chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah and Safwan, from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the Imams (peace be upon them both), who said:
I asked him about forgetfulness (sahw) in the voluntary prayer, and he said, 'There is no obligation upon you (to make it up or prostrate).'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: There is no obligation upon you (ruling of leniency)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for forgetfulness during voluntary prayers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Reported through the chain of al-Ala' and Muhammad ibn Muslim, this hadith from Tahdhib al-Ahkam clarifies that forgetfulness (sahw) in voluntary (nafl) prayers incurs no penalty, reflecting the juristic principle of leniency in non-obligatory acts. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly view that while obligatory prayers require strict adherence to prevent invalidation, nafl prayers serve as a means of spiritual elevation where minor errors are excused to encourage consistent worship.
